title: A phase 2a/b study of DDY391 in participants with Sjögren's disease
official: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase 2a/b study assessing the efficacy, safety and tolerability of DDY391 in participants with Sjögren's Disease
summary:
Main objective: 000000: 

Part A: To evaluate the effect of DDY391 versus placebo in reducing disease activity 

Part B: To evaluate the dose-response of DDY391 versus placebo in reducing disease activity 

000000: 

Part C: To evaluate the efficacy of DDY391 versus placebo in reducing symptom burden
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participants must have a diagnosis of SjD according to the ACR/EULAR 2016 classification criteria at screening.:   Positive anti-Ro (SSA) antibodies at screening. Participants negative for anti-Ro/SSA antibodies are eligible if they have documented previous biopsy within the past two years showing evidence of salivary gland inflammation consistent with SjD. Enrollment of anti-Ro/SSA-negative participants 000000.
2. Inclusion criteria specific for the 000000: constitutional, lymphadenopathy, glandular, articular, cutaneous, renal, hematological and biologic at screening.
3. Female and male participants at least 18 years of age
4. 000000
5. Inclusion criteria specific for the 000000: constitutional, lymphadenopathy, glandular, articular, cutaneous, renal, hematological and biologic at screening.
6. 000000.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of another autoimmune rheumatic disease that is active at screening and constitutes the principal illness
2. Exclusion based on medications being used for SjD:   00000:     Participants taking > 400 mg/day hydroxychloroquine are excluded. Participants taking ≤400 mg/day hydroxychloroquine should be on a stable dose for at least 4 weeks prior to randomization.    000000.   000000.
3. Exclusion based on medications being used for SjD:   00000:    Participants taking > 400 mg/day hydroxychloroquine are excluded. Participants on ≤ 400 mg/day of hydroxychloroquine should be on a stable dose for at least 4 weeks prior to randomization.   000000   000000
4. Prior treatment with any of the following within 3 months prior to randomization: belimumab, abatacept, anti-tumor necrosis factor alpha biologic agents, immunoglobulins, plasmapheresis, intravenous (i.v.) or oral cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil, i.v. or oral cyclosporine A, or any other immunosuppressants (e.g., JAK inhibitors or other kinase inhibitors, IL-2, anti-IL-6, anti-IL-17)
5. Previous treatment with any cell-depleting therapies, including but not limited to anti-CD20, unless ≥ 12 months prior to screening
6. 000000
7. Any viral, bacterial or other infections at the time of screening or randomization, or   history of recurrent clinically significant infection or of recurrent bacterial infection.
8. History of malignancy of any organ system (other than localized non melanoma   carcinoma of the skin or in situ cervical cancer) within the last five years of randomization   or any malignancy not in remission.
